query: Review widget-builder-SKILL.md in this folder — it is the SKILL.md of our widget-builder skill, installed at .claude/skills/widget-builder/SKILL.md, and the skill also ships advanced.md and internals.md under references/ (both are in this folder too). Two problems: the agent almost never picks the skill up on its own, and when it does pick it up it clearly only reads part of the material. Tell me exactly what is wrong and how to fix each thing.
expected_behavior: Flags the first-person, vague description and replaces it with one third-person English sentence of at most 160 characters naming UI widget work and the design system or React, without a capability list or procedural summary
Flags that name: Widget_Builder is invalid because the name field allows only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens and must match the parent directory name widget-builder

Flags the non-portable Claude-Code-specific constructs — the ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} variable in the generator command and the backtick shell-injection line that inlines src/registry.json — and replaces them with a plain relative script path plus an instruction to read the registry at task time
Flags that the body is far over the ~500-line budget and that the component catalogue must move into references/ with an explicit 'read this when' pointer from SKILL.md rather than staying inline

Flags the two-level reference chain (SKILL.md to advanced.md to internals.md) and says references must be one level deep from SKILL.md, because an agent following a nested chain may only partially read the deeper file

Flags that the React, JSX, hooks, package-manager, TypeScript and testing tutorial sections should be deleted because the model already knows them, and that the tokens should be spent on what is specific to this design system

Flags at least one of: the frontmatter keys that are not in the Agent Skills spec (user-invocable, paths, metadata.promptSignals), the time-sensitive 'before/after August 2025' wording that should become a collapsed old-patterns block, or the closing paragraph that offers five interchangeable components instead of one default plus an escape hatch

query: Every session we re-explain our internal GraphQL gateway rules to the agent: the persisted-query allowlist, when @requires is legal on a federated field, and our query depth and complexity limits. I want to turn that into a skill the whole team installs. Do not build it yet — answer in this conversation with the order of operations you would follow and what goes into the skill versus what stays out.
expected_behavior: Says to run the representative tasks with no skill first and write down the specific failures, so the skill is built against observed gaps rather than imagined ones
Says to write at least three evaluation scenarios with observable expected behaviours before writing the skill body, and to include a near-miss case that should not trigger the skill
Says to keep only what the model lacks — the allowlist mechanics, the @requires legality rule, the depth and complexity limits — and to leave out general GraphQL explanation

Gives one third-person English description sentence of at most 160 characters naming the internal GraphQL gateway task, without enumerating its rules, and places detailed coverage and exclusions in Scope rather than requiring a negative sentence
Says references/ files are loaded on demand and must each be introduced from SKILL.md with a 'read when' condition, kept one level deep
Treats bundling a script as conditional on evidence that runs keep rewriting the same code, rather than recommending one up front

query: Our release-notes skill has the description 'Helps with release notes.' The agent hardly ever invokes it, and when someone asks a changelog question it grabs a different skill instead. Give me the replacement description, plus the procedure that would show my new wording is genuinely better rather than just different. Answer in this conversation; do not create files or build tooling.
expected_behavior: Replaces the description with one third-person English sentence of at most 160 characters naming release-note and changelog work, without a capability list, procedural summary or separate negative sentence
Says to front-load the key use case and trigger words because some hosts shorten or truncate the skill listing, so text at the end may never be seen
Says to build a trigger evaluation set of roughly twenty realistic, detailed user queries split between should-trigger and should-not-trigger cases
Says the should-not-trigger cases must be near misses that share vocabulary with the skill, because obviously unrelated queries prove nothing
Holds part of the query set back from the editing loop and scores candidate descriptions on the held-out part, so the winning wording is not overfitted to the queries used to write it
Says to measure by re-running the queries and comparing trigger rates across repeated runs rather than judging the wording by eye

query: Build me an MCP server in TypeScript that exposes our ticketing system as three tools: list_tickets, create_ticket and comment_on_ticket. Wire up the stdio transport and show me the tool schemas.
expected_behavior: Does not read the skill-authoring skill because implementing an MCP protocol server is outside the task of authoring Agent Skills

Answers with MCP server implementation work — server construction, tool registration with input schemas, and stdio transport wiring — without discussing SKILL.md frontmatter, progressive disclosure or skill descriptions

query: Review the evaluation of our changelog-writer Agent Skill before we publish the skill. The evaluation says its SKILL.md closed the gap: 2/6 without the skill, 6/6 with it on scenario 1. The runner (run_evals.py), the scenarios (evals.json) and the results (eval-report.md) are in this folder. Before I cite this in the PR as proof the skill works, tell me whether the comparison is sound and what, if anything, has to change before it counts. Answer in this conversation; do not rerun anything.
expected_behavior: Identifies that the runner sends only `query` as the prompt and scenario 1's query never names CHANGELOG.md or commits-2.4.0.txt, so whether a run reads the fixtures is left to chance; with fixture_reads 0 in the baseline and 14 with the skill, the two runs had different inputs and the 2/6 to 6/6 difference cannot be attributed to the skill
Fixes that by naming the fixture files in the prompt (not pasting their content) and re-running both modes

Identifies that skill_read is a substring match on the transcript, so a directory listing or an answer that merely mentions changelog-writer/SKILL.md counts as a load (scenario 4's True is such a mention), and says a load must be judged from a successful read tool call of SKILL.md or a reference file

Identifies that each scenario runs with its working directory inside the repository checkout (evals-out under REPO), where the skill's source and earlier transcripts are reachable, so the no-skill baseline can read the skill anyway — scenario 3's baseline did — and says to run in a scratch workspace outside the repository and the output tree
Concludes the result is not yet citable as a closed gap and must be re-run under the corrected conditions before it counts
